findings.reason: the implementer must be told whether the digest is read by extending `fetch_tag_messages` to return its annotations map (a deviation from "the same conventions") or by a fifth call, or the "pushes nothing" skip cannot be built as written.
findings.text: §18's skip-check compares the released tree's digest "when that digest equals the latest tag's", and §18 says it annotates each push "with the ambix commit and a sha256 digest of the released tree", but the registry-call paragraph enumerates only `list_registry_tags`, `fetch_tag_messages`, `login_to_ghcr` and `require_oras`, copied "with the same conventions"; the copied `fetch_tag_messages` (imas_codex/graph/ghcr.py:379) returns only the `org.opencontainers.image.description` annotation, so none of the four named calls can read back the digest annotation the skip-check needs, leaving the check with no named mechanism

findings.reason: both routes yield an empty semver tag list and the same `v0.0.0` state, so the wording is imprecise but the behaviour the plan specifies is unchanged.
findings.text: §18 states that `list_registry_tags`'s "package the registry reports as not found read as having no tags" "is how the starting state below is reached", but the JT-60SA package named in the same paragraph is not not-found: it exists and carries the legacy `2026.10.07` tag (`packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:44`), so the no-semver-tag start state is reached by the v-prefix semver filter, not by the not-found branch

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_ambix/maps_cli.py` hides the version state machine, the tag-list sort and the push/pull/status verbs behind one command group; the four GHCR helpers sit under it, not beside it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the GHCR/ORAS owner is named (`imas_codex/graph/ghcr.py`) with the reason for the copy verified: importing `imas_codex.graph.ghcr` executes `imas_codex/graph/__init__.py`, which imports `GraphClient`, `models` and `resolve_neo4j`, so the stated graph-stack cost is real.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §18's "Accounting for the new surface" names the installer's private pull path it retires (merged into `maps pull`), states that `release`/`status` have no existing command to retire, and names the single refusal (`pull` refuses a local tree whose digest matches no released tag) with the reason nothing can retire it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §18 cites the four GHCR helpers it copies from `imas_codex/graph/ghcr.py` and the release state machine from `imas_codex/cli/release.py`, but the cited registry layer exposes no read of the released-tree digest its own skip-check compares against.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no wrapper without its reason: `require_oras`/`login_to_ghcr`/`list_registry_tags`/`fetch_tag_messages` are copied only because ambix takes no imas-codex dependency, and the installer's private pull path is retired into `maps pull` rather than wrapped.
